newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler second quarter earnings fall 53 percent.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler second quarter earnings fall 53 percent.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., hurt by increasing incentives and a month-long engine plant strike, on Friday reported a 53 percent drop in second-quarter earnings to $483 million.

The results, which equalled 70 cents per share, were reduced by $438 million, or 64 cents a share, due to the strike at the automaker's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit, which forced it to idle several truck assembly plants.

Chrysler also said its earnings were hurt by fiercely competitive conditions in the U.S. car and truck market, which pushed up its incentive spending for the April-June quarter to $980 per vehicle from $625 a year earlier and $705 in the first quarter.
The profit was slightly above Wall Street's consensus estimate of 68 cents a share, as published by First Call Corp., but marked a disappointment for high-flying Chrysler.
Nonetheless, investors boosted its stock 50 cents to $35.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The second quarter was a very difficult one for Chrysler. Our results were significantly affected by the UAW strike -- our vehicle shipments were reduced by an estimated 89,000 units," Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton said in a statement.

"While the general economy and consumer confidence continue to look good, increased competition and softer sales have forced us to increase incentives and step up our ongoing efforts to eliminate waste and reduce expenses."
Those actions include a hiring freeze, reduction of overtime and delays on some discretionary capital spenidng projects.
